analysis_type: post-result provenance correction and participant-aware reanalysis

p41_cross_session.caveat: ONE participant. No population claim follows.

participant_identification.caveat: 4 participants, 4 queries per direction; descriptive only

permutation.interpretation: SUPPORTING ONLY. With 4 participant blocks the floor is 1/24 = 0.0417 and the test is coarse. No conclusion in this reanalysis rests on it.

power.note: verifying identity does not fix power

supersedes: CAM-EXP-009.3 remains valid as a within-sequence vs cross-sequence analysis; its participant-provenance interpretation is superseded by this reanalysis.

claims.claim: same sequence L/R closer than cross sequence
claims.evidence: within-session 0.02887 vs cross-participant 0.04937 (ratio 0.585); reproduced exactly from CAM-EXP-009.3

claims.claim: same participant L/R generally closer than different participants
claims.evidence: true at participant-equal weighting (ratio 0.585), but n=4 participants, participant-block permutation p=0.0833 (floor 0.0417), and the effect is not separable from session context

claims.claim: same participant geometry persists across sessions
claims.evidence: p41 cross-session same-side 0.08516 and opposite-side 0.07704, both LARGER than cross-participant 0.04569 and far larger than p41 within-session 0.02113
within-finger bone permutation degrades the distance by +857% (0.0283 -> 0.2706)

claims.claim: strong subject-specific shared anatomy prior justified
claims.evidence: the only same-participant cross-session comparison available is farther apart than different participants, so a person-level template is not supported by this data
within-session bilateral separation is present and 1.89x the reference repeatability; it simply is not attributable to a persistent person-level signature
